name: ToxicChat
description: Despite remarkable advances that large language models have achieved in chatbots, maintaining a non-toxic user-AI interactive environment has become increasingly critical nowadays. However, previous efforts in toxicity detection have been mostly based on benchmarks derived from social media content, leaving the unique challenges inherent to real-world user-AI interactions insufficiently explored. In this work, we introduce ToxicChat, a novel benchmark based on real user queries from an open-source chatbot. This benchmark contains the rich, nuanced phenomena that can be tricky for current toxicity detection models to identify, revealing a significant domain difference compared to social media content. Our systematic evaluation of models trained on existing toxicity datasets has shown their shortcomings when applied to this unique domain of ToxicChat. reputation: A newer benchmark that is gaining attention for toxicity detection in real user-AI chat, but is not yet as widely established as classic toxicity datasets.
notes: Domain shift from social media toxicity datasets is a major issue; likely class imbalance and annotation subjectivity make scores sensitive to thresholding and label definitions.
